# UQDA Core v0.1.10

This release fixes Windows installation isolation from Yggdrasil and adds
source-backed network, configuration and administration documentation. UQDA
remains a separately maintained derivative of Yggdrasil, not an anonymity
system or an independently security-audited network.

## Important: Windows migration from v0.1.9 and older

The old UQDA installer shared MSI identifiers with upstream Yggdrasil. The new
MSI uses a UQDA-only family and refuses to take over an existing legacy UQDA
service automatically. Before installing v0.1.10:

1. Back up `%ProgramData%\UQDA` securely, including any externally referenced
   private-key file. Do not share these backups.
2. Uninstall **UQDA only** through Installed apps. Normal removal preserves
   configuration and identity; do not purge and do not uninstall Yggdrasil.
3. Install the matching new MSI and open a new elevated PowerShell window.
4. Compare the running public key with your previous node identity.

If older UQDA and Yggdrasil packages have already overwritten each other's MSI
registrations, inspect the installed products and backups before removal.
This release cannot safely repair arbitrary historical installer damage.

```powershell
uqda.exe -version
Get-Service UQDA
uqdactl.exe getSelf
uqdactl.exe getPeers
uqdactl.exe doctor
```

New Windows configurations default to `tcp://localhost:19001`. Existing
explicit `AdminListen` settings are preserved; if they still use 9001 and
conflict with another service, back up and change only that setting, then
restart UQDA. Keep administration on loopback, never on a public address.
Loopback does not authenticate local processes as administrators.

Read the [Windows migration and diagnostics guide](https://github.com/Uqda/Core/blob/v0.1.10/docs/windows-installation.md).

## Windows fixes

- Separate MSI upgrade/component identifiers and requested Wintun adapter GUID.
- Do not uninstall the shared Wintun driver when creating a TUN adapter fails.
- Run checked configuration preparation with installer privileges and quoted
  paths; preserve existing identity and reject parse/key-loading errors before
  starting the service. This is not validation of all network conditions.
- Keep the installation directory in machine PATH; open a new terminal after
  installation to pick it up.

The coexistence test validates separate services, binaries, adapter identities,
upgrade/removal and configuration preservation. It does not promise that two
overlays with overlapping IPv6 routes can route every application simultaneously.

## Installation and updates on other platforms

On macOS with the project Homebrew Cask:

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade --cask uqda/core/uqda
sudo uqdactl getSelf
```

For the supported Unix-like installer paths, download and review the updater:

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Uqda/Core/releases/download/v0.1.10/updater.sh
sudo sh updater.sh --version v0.1.10
sudo uqdactl getSelf
```

Use the actual platform configuration/service paths in the
[network guide](https://github.com/Uqda/Core/blob/v0.1.10/docs/NETWORK_GUIDE_AR.md).
Back up identity before changes; do not regenerate configuration merely to update.

## Container package

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/uqda/core:0.1.10
```

The release workflow also updates `ghcr.io/uqda/core:latest`. Four Linux image
platforms are built: amd64, arm64, arm/v7 and arm/v6. The publisher verifies an
anonymous amd64 pull and the binary version; it does not execute every image
architecture on native hardware. Preserve the configuration volume on updates.

every sentence or an uptime guarantee for external peers.

## Verification scope and trust

Pre-release source CI passed Linux/macOS/Windows builds and unit tests,
FreeBSD/OpenBSD cross-builds, lint, documentation checks, dependency scanning,
handshake fuzz smoke tests and Linux mesh scenarios. Windows x64 installation,
coexistence with pinned Yggdrasil 0.5.14, upgrade, legacy-service refusal,
invalid-config repair and uninstall tests passed on the integrated source.

Publication is gated on package builds and the release quality tests, including
installation/query/uninstallation of the final x64 MSI. Windows x86/ARM64 and
router/BSD package builds are not native-device installation certification.
macOS packages are built for Intel and Apple Silicon; package construction is
not a claim of clean installation on every macOS version.

Assets named `-unsigned.msi` or `-unsigned.pkg` lack the corresponding trusted
publisher signature. No signing identity was provisioned by these fixes.
Windows application-control policies or macOS Gatekeeper may still restrict
installation. Do not disable protections or import a self-issued root to bypass
them. An MSI service-start error is separate from publisher trust warnings.

Verify assets against `SHA256SUMS`; its Sigstore bundle and GitHub provenance
attestations identify the release workflow, not a Windows Authenticode publisher.
See [release verification](https://github.com/Uqda/Core/blob/v0.1.10/docs/release-verification.md).

## ملاحظة بالعربية

هذا إصدار إصلاحات وتوثيق، وليس وعدًا باختفاء كل تحذيرات الأنظمة. على Windows
احفظ الهوية ثم أزل UQDA القديمة فقط قبل تثبيت الحزمة الجديدة؛ لا تستخدم purge.
نجاح تشغيل الخدمة لا يعني وجود peers أو وصول كل التطبيقات: افحص `getPeers`
و`doctor` ثم اختبر التطبيق المقصود. الحزم غير الموقعة تبقى موضحة بالاسم.
